transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-18
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jared Kim (Redwood AE), Maya Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Elm Street, Head of ML), Marcus Lee (Elm Street, Eng Mgr), Sandra Hsu (Elm Street, FinOps)

Auto-summary (auto-gen):
- Walkthrough of Console usage analytics focused on per-route dashboards and cost buckets.
- Discussion of mapping Elm Street routes to product lines for chargeback.
- Security brief (SOC2) requested; pilot kickoff and Dedicated sandbox proposed.

Topics
- per-route cost attribution
- SLO/latency monitoring and alerts
- chargeback tags and export formats
- Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs for latency and data isolation

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jared: Okay, hey everyone, thanks for joining. Um this is Jared from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. We got Maya the SE here, she'll run the console demo, and then we'll save time for questions. How's that sound?
[00:08] Priya: Good, yep that works. Thanks for setting this up. We wanted to see how you do per-route costs — we have, like, 12 product routes and wanna bill back to lines.
[00:15] Marcus: And also the SLA implications if we roll to Dedicated later.
[00:19] Sandra: FinOps wants to understand buckets not just per-token but prefix caching effects, yep.
[00:23] Maya: Great. I'll share the console. Quick note — some of the labels in the UI are live telemetry, so you'll see example data; none of your real calls are pulled here.
[00:33] Maya: (screen) So the top nav — Usage -> Routes -> Cost buckets. This is where we correlate per-route token usage to compute class. See here, route "auth-check" maps to the small model family and we attribute short-sequence bursts to the micro-batch path.
[00:45] Priya: Sorry, when you say micro-batch path, is that the continuous batching we talked about?
[00:49] Maya: Yeah, it's essentially the runtime doing continuous batching; we show the effective batch size distribution and the per-token latency cost. Note that short sequences often take the cached KV path which lowers cost.
[00:58] Marcus: Can we split those cached hits vs cold-start tokens in exports?
[01:02] Maya: Yes, the per-route export has columns for cache_hit_count, kv_cache_hits, and cold_token_count. We'll attach a sample CSV after.

[01:14] Jared: Walkthrough of the chargeback mapping — you can create route buckets and tag them with product codes. Sandra, you mentioned you wanted to map by GL account?
[01:22] Sandra: Yeah, GL and then by team. We need to export monthly for our internal billing.
[01:27] Jared: Cool — in Console we have a "Cost Buckets" feature where you can create a bucket, add routes or regex patterns, and attach a billing tag. It supports nested buckets so you can have product -> team.
[01:38] Priya: Regex mapping sounds good, we have dynamic route names. Can it match on header values too?
[01:43] Maya: Not on headers today—mapping is by route name and route metadata. We can do a pre-ingestion transform though; that's part of Dedicated onboarding.

[01:52] Jared: Let's talk SLA and SLO monitoring. Maya, go to the SLO pane.
[01:56] Maya: Right here. You can define SLOs per route: 95th p50 etc, latency buckets, and tie them to alerting policies. We also show cost impact if you tighten SLOs — expected cost delta estimation based on historical distributions.
[02:11] Marcus: How accurate is that cost estimate? Our traffic is spiky by end of month.
[02:16] Maya: The estimator uses percentile-based extrapolation with your traffic histogram. It shows a conservative and optimistic band. For spikes we recommend dedicated capacity or autoscale policies with burst.

[02:27] Priya: Okay can we demo a snapshot where a route's latency climbs and it flips to a fallback model?
[02:31] Maya: Sure — here's a simulated incident in the timeline. You can see automatic fallback triggered from gpt-small-quant to gpt-micro-variant. The dashboard flags the increase in token cost and the route's error rate.
[02:42] Priya: I see the fallback note, it's labeled "auto-variant-fallback" — sometimes our infra names are a bit different, will that match?
[02:47] Jared: You can customize the label and the fallback policy per route. Also, for Dedicated you can pin variants to avoid auto-fallback.

[02:55] Sandra: Quick question on compliance — we need audit logs with user-level actions, and KMS-backed key management.
[03:01] Jared: Yep, SOC2 is supported; we provide audit logs, SSO/SAML, and KMS integration for Private and Dedicated. We can also do customer-managed keys in the Private on-prem flow.
[03:14] Sandra: Do you retain raw request payloads? For us PII is an issue.
[03:19] Maya: By default, hosted mode keeps minimal telemetry and binds raw payload retention to your retention policy. For strict PII requirements we recommend Private deployment or Dedicated with data retention turned off.

[03:29] Marcus: I wanted to drill into the export. Can you show a monthly export with per-route cost and the token breakdown?
[03:34] Maya: Yep exporting now. (small pause) The CSV includes: route_name, product_tag, token_count, cache_hits, cold_token_count, compute_seconds, gpu_fraction, cost_usd_estimate. We also output an attribution GUID so you can join to your billing system.
[03:49] Priya: Nice. Does the export show quantization tier? We run mixed precision on some models.
[03:54] Maya: We include model_variant and quant_tier columns. If you use mixed quantization or custom kernels we'll surface that in the export as variant metadata.

[04:04] Jared: Let's talk pilot scope. Proposed pilot is: map 6 routes, run a two-week telemetry capture, demo chargeback export and SLO alerts, then brief FinOps with a 30-min review. Thoughts?
[04:14] Sandra: That timeline sounds reasonable, as long as we get the export in a canonical format so our CFO can review.
[04:20] Marcus: We'll need infra to validate network rules for Dedicated sandbox — who owns that?
[04:24] Jared: We'll coordinate. For Dedicated we have a network checklist — VPC peering, firewall rules, and optional on-prem connectors. We'll send that.

[04:33] Priya: One more technical: how do you attribute tokens when a route fans out to multiple models — e.g., we call a re-ranker after a generator?
[04:40] Maya: Great question. We attribute at the request-edge by default: the initial route gets generator tokens, and the re-ranker route logs its own tokens as a separate route with a parent_id linking to the initial request. That parent linkage is in the export so you can roll-up per transaction.
[04:55] Marcus: So we can cost a whole transaction across two routes by joining parent_id. Perfect.

[05:02] (silence while Maya toggles panels)
[05:10] Maya: Here's the "Route Heatmap" view — it shows token volume by hour with color for cost density. You can filter by model family or quant tier.
[05:19] Priya: That helps for spotting hot windows. Is there a way to compare before/after quantization across the same route?
[05:25] Maya: You can pick two time ranges and the console will show a delta view, including cost per 1k tokens and latency percentile shifts.

[05:34] Sandra: On chargeback, will the GL tag be a free text or enforced enum?
[05:38] Jared: We allow both. For your finance safety we recommend pushing an allowed-list via the UI so exports are consistent.

[05:45] Priya: Security follow-up — can you do a brief on how RBAC maps to routes? We need separation so product teams only see their routes.
[05:52] Maya: RBAC is role and route based. You can create a role tied to route patterns. For example, product-A role can only view routes matching ^/product-A/.* and only see aggregated cost for others as "masked".
[06:05] Marcus: Nice. That will help with least privilege.

[06:10] Jared: Moving into slightly deeper stuff — batching and cache behavior. Maya, show the continuous batching analytics.
[06:15] Maya: This panel shows effective batch size vs latency; you can choose target latency SLO and see recommended batch sizing. Also, the console suggests cache TTL heuristics based on prefix reuse.
[06:26] Priya: How often do you tune those TTL heuristics? Our prefixes change a lot with session tokens.
[06:31] Maya: TTLs are suggestions from the optimizer; you can lock them per route. During pilot we tune heuristics weekly.

[06:39] Sandra: For cost modeling, can we simulate a 10% traffic increase and see predicted cost delta?
[06:44] Maya: Yes — use the "What-if" tool. You can bump traffic by percent or inject a synthetic spike and the model will show cost band and forecasted SLA breaching risk.

[06:55] Priya: Can we integrate those forecasts into our internal FinOps pipeline? Like an API?
[06:59] Jared: There's an API endpoint for exports and forecasts — documented in the API section. We'll share keys for the trial.

[07:05] Marcus: One more thing on Dedicated — if we want both low-latency and lower cost, can we have mixed pools?
[07:11] Maya: Yes, Redwood Dedicated supports heterogeneous pools: latency-priority and cost-priority. Smart routing can send critical traffic to latency pool and best-effort to cost pool.
[07:21] Priya: How do you handle model variants across those pools?
[07:24] Maya: We keep a catalog of variant compatibility. If strict pinning is needed, you can lock a route to a pool + variant.

[07:31] Jared: All right, let's surface some potential concerns—Sandra, anything else from FinOps?
[07:36] Sandra: Just auditability and a reliable monthly export. Also we want to be able to detect anomalies where a route suddenly spikes cost due to a prompt change. Do you have anomaly alerts?
[07:45] Maya: Yup — anomaly detection on cost per route is built-in. You can set sensitivity and channels (Slack, PagerDuty). It also ties to the route history so you can rewind and compare.
[07:56] Marcus: Do you provide per-token flamegraphs or anything for debugging cost hotspots?
[08:00] Maya: There's a "token waterfall" view — it's not a flamegraph per se but shows how tokens are consumed across prompts, system messages, and responses. It helps surface cases where instruction prompts are accidentally huge.
[08:11] Priya: That would have helped with a past incident, haha.

[08:16] Jared: Okay, wrapping to next steps. We propose: Jared sends security pack and pilot scope doc, Maya sends sample CSV and mapping guide, and we'll schedule the pilot kickoff with Marcus.
[08:27] Priya: Sounds good — and Marcus will invite our infra folks. Sandra will be on the FinOps review.
[08:33] Marcus: I'll set tentative calendar for July 1 at 10am and send invites.
[08:38] Sandra: Please include cost export template for CFO review.

[08:42] Jared: Great. Any final questions?
[08:45] Priya: Quick one: who is the dedicated contact for escalation?
[08:48] Jared: For the pilot it's Maya for technical and I'll take account-level escalations. For Dedicated we assign an onboarding SE and a Solutions Architect.
[08:58] Marcus: Good, thanks.

[09:01] (meeting ends)
